tasks.short: Receive payments, record receipts, arrange deposits, and reconcile bank credits.

steps.what: Receive cash, checks, and vouchers; count and verify against payment evidence.
Enter receipts and allocate customer accounts in the {ERP}.
Prepare deposit paperwork and reconcile its total to the receipt record.
Secure and hand over deposit instruments; obtain deposit confirmation.
Match bank credits in the {ERP} to receipts and deposit confirmation.
Investigate unmatched deposits and send supported correction requests to the accountant.

tasks.design: Configure receipt capture and exact bank matching in the {ERP}; generate deposit schedules from receipt records. A small exception view links receipts, deposit confirmation, and bank credits, with correction requests passed into the accountant's approval flow. People retain physical custody and deposit handover.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical custody cannot be digitised. Separate receipt entry, deposit paperwork, and bank records also create duplicate work.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing receipt and bank-matching features cover much of the work. AI-assisted coding reduces the effort of building deposit templates and connecting exception records.
tasks.still_hard: Cash shortages, uncertain payer identity, check clearance, and physical security remain operational problems.
tasks.human_edge: Count physical instruments, protect custody, and establish what happened when money is missing.

ambition.what: Daily deposit timing recommendations for cash-accepting sites

tasks.altitude: Physical handling still occupies much of the week, but duplicate entry and matching shrink. The clerk gains time to recommend deposit timing; treasury retains custody policy and banking authority.

reach.task: Assess when deposited receipts become available cash.
reach.learn: Bank cutoffs, clearance periods, cash availability, and deposit costs.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit supports automatic bank matching using references, IBANs, or invoice numbers, with unmatched lines handled separately.
Deposit schedule generation is deterministic; software does not replace physical custody.

assumptions: This describes a cash-accepting site; checks are handled only where still received.
Direct customer bank transfers bypass physical receipt and deposit steps.
Vouchers are recorded or redeemed under their settlement rules; only bankable instruments enter deposits.
Time shares are illustrative task effort, not measured company data.
Build ranges cover one receipt process and bank connection, with existing equipment.
Access work includes GDPR controls and any employee consultation required by national rules.
unknowns: Payment mix, physical receipt volume, and deposit arrangements.
Whether the {ERP} already supports receipt capture and bank matching.
Who holds custody and who approves correcting entries.
Applicable national consultation requirements and access lead times.
research_questions: Can receipt identifiers survive deposit batching and appear in bank settlement records?
Can configuration produce the required deposit paperwork without custom code?
new_work: Review captured receipt details before recording.
Maintain deposit templates, matching rules, and bank connections.
Resolve unmatched credits and monitor failed imports.
Reconcile physical custody evidence with digital records.

tasks.short: Classify financial documents by account, tax treatment, cost centre, and other required codes.

steps.what: Collect financial documents from the shared mailbox and document queue.
Read documents and enter relevant financial fields in the {ERP}.

loop.input: Unstructured financial documents; structured documents bypass the model.
loop.output: Typed document fields with page references and uncertainty flags.
loop.check: Validate field types, duplicate identifiers, known counterparties, and applicable total and tax arithmetic.
loop.stop: One extraction and one repair attempt per document; failed checks route to manual entry.
loop.why_not_simpler: Structured imports and configured capture run first; varied free-text layouts may still need bounded extraction.

steps.what: Select account, tax, and cost-centre codes using company procedures.
Investigate ambiguous descriptions, allocations, or tax treatment and propose codes.
Approve unusual coding or return the proposal for clarification.
Save completed coding and attach the source document in the {ERP}.

tasks.design: Route documents into the {ERP}, import structured fields, and use bounded extraction only for unsupported document layouts. Configure coding rules from approved account and allocation policies, sending ambiguous cases to the clerk and unusual decisions to the accountant. Save source links and coding history alongside each record.
tasks.previous_blocker: Document formats vary, coding policies contain exceptions, and historical supplier codes can conceal mistakes.
tasks.enabler_now: Configured capture and coding rules already handle repeatable cases. Small extraction components and validation checks are now cheaper to build and adapt.
tasks.still_hard: Mixed-purpose expenditure, new tax treatments, and disputed allocations need context beyond the document.
tasks.human_edge: Understand the business purpose of spending and recognise when a familiar coding pattern is wrong.

ambition.what: A monthly coding-quality clinic for budget holders

tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time transcribing and selecting routine codes, and more time resolving ambiguous expenditure. They can recommend policy clarifications; the accountant retains accounting and tax policy decisions.

reach.task: Explain recurring cost-centre misallocations to budget holders.
reach.learn: Budget structures, allocation drivers, and management reporting dimensions.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit reads invoice documents and identifies suppliers using registration, VAT, and bank details.
The Huuskes case documents automated invoice processing with Medius; it does not establish equivalent results for general document coding.
Approved coding rules can automate repeatable classifications while ambiguous accounting treatment remains with people.

assumptions: Routine documents have approved coding rules; exceptions do not automatically create new rules.
Time shares include conditional exception and approval work averaged across the task.
The design saves coding records; payment release remains a separate action.
Build ranges cover one entity, a bounded document set, and an existing account master.
GDPR applies to document processing; model use requires appropriate access, retention, and EU AI Act literacy.
Access estimates include employee consultation where national rules require it; statutory timelines may exceed the range.
unknowns: Document types, languages, volumes, and structured-input coverage.
Existing capture, coding, and approval capabilities in the {ERP}.
Quality of coding rules and historical classifications.
Permitted model processing locations and document retention rules.
research_questions: Which document families can use structured imports or configured capture without a model?
Can approved rules explain each code and detect conflicting mappings?
How often do valid-looking extracted fields differ from the source?
new_work: Review extracted fields and repair failed validation.
Maintain approved mappings and effective dates.
Sample routine classifications for silent errors.
Maintain extraction templates and evaluate changes on representative documents.
Run the coding-quality clinic and track recurring causes.

tasks.short: Calculate amounts due, interest, balances, discounts, and principal using approved financial terms.

steps.what: Retrieve transaction balances and schedules from the {ERP}.
Look up applicable rates, dates, discounts, and calculation conventions.
Resolve ambiguous terms and approve departures from standard calculation rules.
Calculate amounts using {ERP} functions or a supporting {SPREADSHEET}.
Check results against source balances, rounding rules, and expected movements.
Record checked amounts and retain calculation support in the {ERP}.

tasks.design: Configure effective-dated terms and calculation functions in the {ERP}, with explicit rounding and date conventions. A deterministic check on the {DATA_PLATFORM} validates balances and movements, routing failures for review before recording results. Ambiguous contractual terms remain with the accountant.
tasks.previous_blocker: Supporting workbooks bridge missing configuration, while rates and conventions sit in documents rather than maintained fields.
tasks.enabler_now: The arithmetic already exists in standard software. Faster configuration support and small deterministic checks make retiring local workbooks more practical.
tasks.still_hard: Selecting the legally and contractually correct basis can be harder than calculating the amount.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise when standard terms do not fit the transaction and obtain an authoritative interpretation.
tasks.altitude: Routine calculation and rekeying largely leave the week. The clerk can recommend which discounts merit treasury attention; payment authority and interpretation of unusual terms stay with existing approvers.

reach.task: Compare early-payment discounts with the cost of cash.
reach.learn: Annualised discount returns, liquidity constraints, and payment scheduling.

evidence.claim: Balances, discounts, interest, and principal calculations can use deterministic formulas and configured financial terms.
The digest provides no documented case specifically establishing results for this calculation task.

assumptions: The task concerns routine financial calculations, not equity valuation or investment advice.
Standard terms can be stored as structured, effective-dated fields; ambiguous terms are excluded from automatic use.
The {ERP} handles routine calculations, with supporting workbooks used for gaps and checks.
Human review covers failed checks; validated standard results can proceed under approved rules.
Build ranges cover one entity and a limited formula set, including access and any consultation required by national rules.
GDPR applies to personal financial data; the proposed calculation path needs no model.
unknowns: Calculation types, currencies, and transaction volumes.
Applicable national rules and contractual interest conventions.
Who approves rates, exceptions, and changes to formulas.
Whether the recording action updates a working record or posts a journal.
research_questions: Can configuration replace each supporting workbook?
Which independent identities and boundary cases validate the calculations?
Can terms changes be versioned without altering historical results?
new_work: Maintain effective-dated rates, terms, and conventions.
Review failed checks and ambiguous contracts.
Validate formula changes against independent examples.
Monitor missing inputs and stale rate tables.
Prepare discount recommendations if the ambition is adopted.

tasks.short: Reconcile financial records, investigate differences, and report supported discrepancies.

steps.what: Export ledger balances and collect bank statements and supporting records.
Compare records in a {SPREADSHEET} and identify unmatched items or balance differences.
Read supporting documents and remittance messages to explain discrepancies.

loop.input: Unmatched records and linked supporting documents or remittance messages.
loop.output: Evidence-linked explanations, proposed matches, and draft requests for missing evidence.
loop.check: Verify cited records, amounts, currencies, dates, uniqueness, and aggregate totals; a person accepts proposed explanations.
loop.stop: One analysis and one repair attempt per discrepancy; missing evidence or failed checks return to the clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Exact rules run first; free-text references and explanations can still require reading across documents.

steps.what: Obtain missing evidence and resolve disputed explanations with relevant parties.
Approve supported correcting entries or reject the proposed treatment.
Post approved corrections and update reconciliation status in the {ERP}.
Compile reconciliation results and report outstanding discrepancies to the financial controller.

tasks.design: Feed controlled extracts into the {DATA_PLATFORM}, reconcile records with deterministic rules, and publish exceptions through the {WORKFLOW} and {BI}. A bounded reading loop proposes explanations from linked evidence, while people handle disputed facts and approve correcting entries. The {ERP} posts approved corrections and returns status to the reconciliation report.
tasks.previous_blocker: Record identifiers differ across sources, supporting evidence arrives late, and reconciliation workbooks lose the link between differences and corrections.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing bank matching covers straightforward cases. Smaller integrations, traceable exception records, and bounded document reading now cost less to assemble.
tasks.still_hard: Missing evidence, timing differences, net settlements, and disputed accounting treatment remain. Matching cannot establish that an underlying transaction was legitimate.
tasks.human_edge: Challenge plausible explanations, obtain credible evidence, and distinguish timing differences from errors or suspicious activity.

ambition.what: Daily escalation of ageing reconciliation breaks

tasks.altitude: The week shifts from comparing rows to resolving breaks and preparing supported corrections. The clerk can prioritise escalation using agreed thresholds; the accountant retains correction approval and the controller retains close sign-off.

reach.task: Assess whether an unresolved break requires a period-end adjustment.
reach.learn: Cutoff, materiality, accruals, evidence standards, and journal controls.

reach.task: Analyse recurring causes of reconciliation failures.
reach.learn: Data lineage, stable identifiers, reconciliation metrics, and source-quality checks.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit supports rule-based bank matching and separates unmatched lines for handling.
Deterministic reconciliation can validate totals and unique matches; document-based explanations still need evidence checks.
The digest does not document autonomous resolution of general ledger discrepancies.

assumptions: This covers routine bank and ledger reconciliations, not a full statutory audit.
Configured {ERP} matching is reused first; custom rules cover cross-source gaps.
Automatic matching requires exact amounts, consistent currencies, and unambiguous record use; other cases remain exceptions.
Correcting entries require approval; proposed model matches never directly authorise postings.
Build ranges cover a limited account set and a small number of source connections.
GDPR controls cover financial records containing personal data, and EU AI Act literacy applies to model users.
Access estimates include consultation where national rules require it; customer-specific approval timelines can exceed the range.
unknowns: Reconciliation types, account counts, source systems, and break volumes.
Existing identifiers, matching rules, and export completeness.
Materiality thresholds and journal approval arrangements.
Evidence access, retention periods, and permitted model processing.
Applicable national consultation requirements and access lead times.
research_questions: Which reconciliations can be handled entirely by existing {ERP} configuration?
Can source completeness be checked independently before matching begins?
How will matching rules handle duplicates, reversals, net settlements, and period boundaries?
Does bounded reading reduce investigation time without increasing accepted false explanations?
new_work: Monitor source completeness, import failures, and duplicate processing.
Review proposed explanations and maintain evidence links.
Maintain matching rules and validate rule changes.
Track unresolved breaks, owners, and ageing.
Check model outputs for unsupported explanations.
Investigate recurring source-data problems with adjacent teams.

role.altitude: Routine entry, arithmetic, and comparison shrink, while physical custody, evidence gathering, and accounting exceptions remain. The clerk gains scope to recommend operational improvements and prioritise exceptions within agreed limits; payment release and accounting policy authority do not automatically change.
reach: Treasurer: assess deposit availability and early-payment discounts.
Accountant: prepare evidence-based period-end adjustment proposals.
Budget analyst: explain recurring expenditure misallocations.
Business intelligence analyst: identify recurring reconciliation failures.
skills_to_grow: Configure financial rules and effective dates.
Validate structured imports and reconciliation completeness.
Read contracts and recognise accounting exceptions.
Review extracted data against source evidence.
Understand GDPR, applicable national rules, and EU AI Act literacy duties.
role.ambitious_version: Provide a daily financial-records quality service: identify unresolved receipt, coding, calculation, and reconciliation issues, explain their operational impact, and recommend specific actions to the authorised decision makers.
